title: Britain and its colonies switch to the Gregorian calendar
summary: Across Great Britain and its American colonies, Wednesday 2 September 1752 was followed directly by Thursday 14 September. Eleven days were dropped and the legal year now began on 1 January.
reason: Britain had kept the Julian calendar long after most of Catholic Europe, which made dates in trade and diplomacy confusing.
significance: It aligned the English speaking world with the calendar most of the world uses today.

title: Samuel Johnson publishes his Dictionary
summary: Samuel Johnson's A Dictionary of the English Language was published in London. It defined about 40,000 words and illustrated them with quotations from English literature.
reason: London booksellers wanted an authoritative English dictionary comparable to those of the French and Italian academies, and hired Johnson to write it.
significance: It shaped English lexicography and remained the standard dictionary until the Oxford English Dictionary.
wikipedia: A Dictionary of the English Language

title: Great earthquake destroys Lisbon
summary: A massive earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, destroyed most of Lisbon on All Saints' Day. Tens of thousands of people died.
reason: A sudden rupture along the plate boundary in the Atlantic southwest of Portugal released enormous energy close to the densely built capital.
significance: It shook European faith in divine providence, inspired Enlightenment debate and led to early modern seismology and urban planning.

title: Prisoners die in the Black Hole of Calcutta
summary: After the Nawab of Bengal captured Fort William, British prisoners were locked overnight in a small cell of the fort. Many of them died from heat and suffocation.
reason: Siraj ud-Daulah attacked Calcutta because the East India Company had fortified the town and defied his authority.
significance: The incident became a British rallying cry that helped justify the campaign that led to Plassey.

title: Battle of Plassey gives the British control of Bengal
summary: Robert Clive's East India Company army defeated the much larger force of Siraj ud-Daulah, Nawab of Bengal. Much of the Nawab's army, under Mir Jafar, did not fight.
reason: Clive had secretly agreed with Mir Jafar to make him Nawab in exchange for his betrayal, after the Nawab had taken Calcutta.
significance: It began British political dominance in India.

title: British defeat the French on the Plains of Abraham
summary: James Wolfe's British army climbed the cliffs above the St. Lawrence and defeated Montcalm's French force outside Quebec City. Both commanders were mortally wounded.
reason: Britain sought to conquer New France during the Seven Years' War, and Quebec was its key fortress.
significance: It led to the fall of Quebec and the end of French rule in Canada.
wikipedia: Battle of the Plains of Abraham

title: Afghans crush the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat
summary: The army of Ahmad Shah Durrani, joined by Indian allies, destroyed the Maratha army at Panipat north of Delhi. Tens of thousands were killed in the battle and its aftermath.
reason: The Marathas had expanded into northern India and the Punjab, clashing with Durrani's ambitions there.
significance: It halted Maratha expansion and left a power vacuum that the British later exploited.

title: Treaty of Paris ends the Seven Years' War
summary: Britain, France and Spain signed a peace treaty in Paris. France ceded Canada and lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, and Spain ceded Florida.
reason: After years of global war, the exhausted powers sought peace on terms that reflected British victories.
significance: It made Britain the dominant colonial power in North America and India.

title: East India Company wins the Battle of Buxar
summary: Company forces under Hector Munro defeated the combined armies of Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.
reason: Mir Qasim had tried to assert independence from the Company and allied with other Indian rulers against it.
significance: It confirmed Company supremacy in eastern India.

title: British Parliament passes the Stamp Act
summary: Parliament imposed a direct tax on the American colonies, requiring stamped paper for legal documents, newspapers and other printed items.
reason: Britain wanted the colonies to help pay for troops stationed in America after the costly Seven Years' War.
significance: Colonial protest under the slogan of no taxation without representation set the path toward the American Revolution.

title: Treaty of Allahabad grants the Diwani of Bengal
summary: Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the right to collect revenue in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
reason: After defeat at Buxar, the emperor needed Company protection, and Robert Clive wanted a legal basis for Company rule.
significance: It turned a trading company into a territorial power in India.

title: James Watt patents his separate condenser
summary: James Watt received a patent for a steam engine with a separate condenser, which greatly reduced the fuel the engine needed.
reason: Watt found while repairing a Newcomen engine that heating and cooling the same cylinder wasted most of the steam.
significance: Efficient steam power drove the Industrial Revolution.

title: Cook's expedition observes the transit of Venus from Tahiti
summary: James Cook, Charles Green and others recorded the passage of Venus across the Sun from Point Venus in Tahiti.
reason: The Royal Society sent the expedition so that timings from distant places could be used to measure the distance from the Earth to the Sun.
significance: It was part of the first great international scientific project and opened the Pacific voyages of Cook.
wikipedia: 1769 transit of Venus observed from Tahiti

title: British soldiers kill five colonists in the Boston Massacre
summary: British soldiers fired into a hostile crowd on King Street in Boston, killing five men.
reason: Troops had been stationed in Boston to enforce unpopular taxes, and tension with residents had been building for months.
significance: Patriot propaganda used it to turn colonial opinion against British rule.

title: James Cook lands at Botany Bay
summary: The Endeavour anchored in Botany Bay and Cook's crew made their first landing on the east coast of Australia, meeting the Gweagal people.
reason: Cook was charting the unknown southern lands after observing the transit of Venus.
significance: It led to the British claim on eastern Australia and later colonisation.

title: James Bruce reaches the source of the Blue Nile
summary: Scottish traveller James Bruce reached the springs at Gish Abay in Ethiopia, which he took to be the source of the Nile.
reason: Bruce had travelled through Abyssinia hoping to solve the old puzzle of the origin of the Nile.
significance: His account brought Ethiopia to wide European attention.

title: Somerset v Stewart rules against forced removal of a slave
summary: Lord Mansfield ruled that James Somerset, an enslaved man brought to England, could not be forcibly taken out of the country to be sold.
reason: Abolitionist Granville Sharp backed Somerset's case to test whether slavery had legal standing in England.
significance: It was widely taken to mean slavery had no basis in English law and strengthened the abolition movement.

title: Russia, Prussia and Austria agree the First Partition of Poland
summary: Russia, Prussia and Austria signed agreements in Saint Petersburg to annex about a third of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
reason: The neighbouring powers wanted to keep a balance among themselves while exploiting the weakness of the Commonwealth.
significance: It began the process that erased Poland from the map by 1795.

title: James Cook's ships cross the Antarctic Circle
summary: HMS Resolution and HMS Adventure became the first known ships to cross the Antarctic Circle.
reason: Cook was searching for a great southern continent that geographers believed must exist.
significance: It showed that any southern continent lay far to the south, beyond habitable lands.
place: Southern Ocean, south of the Indian Ocean

title: Colonists dump British tea in the Boston Tea Party
summary: Members of the Sons of Liberty, some disguised as Mohawks, boarded ships in Boston Harbor and threw 342 chests of East India Company tea into the water.
reason: They protested the Tea Act, which they saw as taxation without representation.
significance: Britain's harsh response with the Intolerable Acts pushed the colonies toward revolution.

title: Treaty of Kucuk Kaynarca ends a Russo-Turkish war
summary: The Ottoman Empire made peace with Russia, recognising the independence of the Crimean Khanate and giving Russia ports on the Black Sea.
reason: Russia had won a series of decisive victories over the Ottomans by land and sea.
significance: It marked the beginning of Ottoman decline relative to Russia and the start of the Eastern Question.

title: American Revolutionary War begins at Lexington and Concord
summary: British troops marching to seize colonial weapons at Concord clashed with militiamen at Lexington and then at Concord's North Bridge, and were harried all the way back to Boston.
reason: Tension over British control of Massachusetts had reached a breaking point after the Intolerable Acts.
significance: These first shots began the war that created the United States.

title: Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations
summary: Adam Smith's An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations was published in London.
reason: Smith wanted to explain how division of labour and free markets produce prosperity, against the mercantilist policies of his time.
significance: It founded modern economics.

title: Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence
summary: The Second Continental Congress in Philadelphia approved the Declaration of Independence, announcing that the thirteen colonies were free states.
reason: After a year of war, colonial leaders concluded that reconciliation with Britain was impossible.
significance: It created the United States and set out ideals of equality and rights that inspired later revolutions.

title: James Cook is killed at Kealakekua Bay
summary: Captain James Cook was killed in a fight with Hawaiians at Kealakekua Bay after he tried to take the chief Kalaniopuu hostage over a stolen boat.
reason: Relations soured after Cook's ships returned unexpectedly for repairs, straining local resources.
significance: It ended the life of the greatest explorer of the Pacific, whose voyages had opened Hawaii to the world.

title: William Herschel discovers Uranus
summary: From his garden in Bath, William Herschel observed an object he first took for a comet. It proved to be a new planet, later named Uranus.
reason: Herschel was systematically surveying the sky with telescopes he built himself.
significance: It was the first planet discovered with a telescope and doubled the known size of the Solar System.
place: New King Street, Bath, United Kingdom

title: Tupac Amaru II is executed in Cusco
summary: Spanish authorities executed Tupac Amaru II, leader of the largest indigenous uprising in colonial Spanish America, in the main square of Cusco.
reason: He had led a rebellion against forced labour, taxes and abuses by colonial officials.
significance: He became a lasting symbol of indigenous resistance and Latin American independence.

title: Cornwallis surrenders at Yorktown
summary: The British army of Lord Cornwallis surrendered to American and French forces after a siege at Yorktown, Virginia.
reason: Washington and Rochambeau trapped Cornwallis while a French fleet blocked rescue by sea.
significance: It effectively decided the American Revolutionary War.

title: Rama I founds the Chakri dynasty of Siam
summary: General Chao Phraya Chakri took the throne of Siam as King Rama I, and soon moved the capital across the river to Bangkok.
reason: King Taksin had been deposed amid unrest, and the leading general was invited to rule.
significance: The Chakri dynasty still reigns in Thailand.

title: Laki fissure eruption begins in Iceland
summary: A long fissure at Laki began erupting lava and toxic gases, an eruption that continued for eight months.
reason: Volcanic activity along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge opened a fissure in southern Iceland.
significance: It killed a large part of Iceland's livestock and population and caused deadly haze and crop failures across Europe.

title: Treaty of Paris recognises American independence
summary: Britain and the United States signed a peace treaty in Paris. Britain recognised the independence of the United States with borders reaching the Mississippi.
reason: After Yorktown, Britain decided to end a costly war it could not win.
significance: It formally established the United States as an independent nation.

title: First free flight of humans in a hot air balloon
summary: Pilatre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes flew a Montgolfier hot air balloon over Paris for about 25 minutes.
reason: The Montgolfier brothers had shown that heated air could lift a balloon and wanted to prove humans could fly safely.
significance: It was the first human flight.
place: Chateau de la Muette, Paris, France

title: William Jones founds the Asiatic Society in Calcutta
summary: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta to study the history, languages and sciences of Asia.
reason: Jones believed Europeans in India should study its classical languages and texts in depth.
significance: It launched modern Indology and, through Jones, the idea of the Indo-European language family.

title: Treaty of Mangalore ends the Second Anglo-Mysore War
summary: Tipu Sultan of Mysore and the East India Company made peace at Mangalore, each returning conquered territory.
reason: Neither side could win outright, and the Company had lost its French support after peace in Europe.
significance: It was the last time an Indian ruler dictated terms to the Company as an equal.

title: Mont Blanc is climbed for the first time
summary: Jacques Balmat and Michel-Gabriel Paccard reached the summit of Mont Blanc, the highest peak of the Alps.
reason: The scientist Horace-Benedict de Saussure had offered a reward for the first ascent.
significance: It is considered the birth of modern mountaineering.

title: The United States Constitution is signed
summary: Delegates to the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia signed the new Constitution of the United States.
reason: The Articles of Confederation had left the national government too weak to tax, defend or regulate commerce.
significance: It became the oldest written national constitution still in use.
wikipedia: Signing of the United States Constitution

title: First Fleet establishes a British colony at Sydney Cove
summary: Arthur Phillip raised the British flag at Sydney Cove, where the convicts and marines of the First Fleet founded the colony of New South Wales.
reason: Britain needed a new place to send convicts after losing the American colonies.
significance: It began European settlement of Australia and the dispossession of its Aboriginal peoples.

title: Mutiny on the Bounty
summary: Fletcher Christian and part of the crew seized HMS Bounty near Tonga and set Captain William Bligh adrift with loyal men in a small boat.
reason: After months in Tahiti, the crew resented a return to harsh discipline under Bligh.
significance: Bligh's 6,700 km open boat voyage and the mutineers' settlement of Pitcairn became legendary.

title: George Washington is inaugurated as first US president
summary: George Washington took the oath of office on the balcony of Federal Hall in New York City.
reason: He had been unanimously elected under the new Constitution.
significance: It began the American presidency and a tradition of peaceful constitutional government.
place: Federal Hall, New York City, United States

title: Deputies swear the Tennis Court Oath
summary: Locked out of their hall, deputies of the Third Estate met in a tennis court at Versailles and swore not to separate until France had a constitution.
reason: The king's government resisted the Third Estate's claim to be the National Assembly.
significance: It was the first open defiance of royal authority in the French Revolution.

title: Parisians storm the Bastille
summary: A crowd of Parisians attacked and captured the Bastille fortress and prison, seeking its gunpowder.
reason: Fear that the king would crush the National Assembly, together with high bread prices, drove Paris into revolt.
significance: It became the symbol of the French Revolution and the end of absolute monarchy.

title: France adopts the Declaration of the Rights of Man
summary: The National Constituent Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.
reason: Deputies wanted to state the principles of a new order after abolishing feudal privileges.
significance: It became a founding text of human rights and liberal democracy.
wikipedia: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen

title: Poland-Lithuania adopts the Constitution of 3 May
summary: The Great Sejm in Warsaw adopted a constitution that strengthened the monarchy and abolished the liberum veto.
reason: Reformers wanted to save the Commonwealth from paralysis and foreign domination after the first partition.
significance: It was Europe's first modern written constitution.

title: Bois Caiman ceremony launches the Haitian Revolution
summary: Enslaved people of northern Saint-Domingue gathered at Bois Caiman for a Vodou ceremony led by Dutty Boukman, where they planned a revolt. The uprising broke out a week later.
reason: Brutal plantation slavery and news of revolutionary ideals from France fuelled the plot.
significance: It began the only successful slave revolution in history.

title: Mozart's The Magic Flute premieres in Vienna
summary: Mozart's opera The Magic Flute, with a libretto by Emanuel Schikaneder, premiered at the Theater auf der Wieden. Mozart conducted.
reason: Schikaneder's popular theatre wanted a German language opera mixing comedy, fantasy and Masonic ideals.
significance: It became one of the most performed operas in the world.
place: Theater auf der Wieden, Vienna, Austria

title: The US Bill of Rights is ratified
summary: Virginia's approval completed ratification of the first ten amendments to the United States Constitution.
reason: Opponents of the Constitution had demanded explicit protections for individual liberties.
significance: It guaranteed freedoms of speech, religion, press and fair trial that shape American law.

title: Unzen landslide and tsunami kill about 15,000 in Japan
summary: An earthquake caused the collapse of Mount Mayuyama near Shimabara, sending debris into the Ariake Sea and raising a tsunami.
reason: Months of volcanic activity at Mount Unzen had weakened the neighbouring dome.
significance: It was Japan's deadliest volcanic disaster.

title: French revolutionaries win the cannonade of Valmy
summary: French forces under Kellermann and Dumouriez stopped the Prussian advance on Paris in an artillery duel at Valmy.
reason: Prussia and Austria had invaded to restore Louis XVI's power.
significance: It saved the Revolution, and the Republic was proclaimed the next day.

title: Louis XVI is guillotined
summary: The deposed king of France was beheaded on the Place de la Revolution in Paris.
reason: The National Convention found him guilty of conspiring against the nation.
significance: Killing a king shocked Europe and widened the war against revolutionary France.
place: Place de la Concorde, Paris, France

title: Qianlong Emperor receives the Macartney embassy
summary: The Qianlong Emperor received Lord Macartney, Britain's first envoy to China, at the summer retreat of Chengde.
reason: Britain wanted to open China to wider trade and a permanent embassy.
significance: China's refusal of these requests foreshadowed the conflicts of the Opium Wars.

title: French National Convention abolishes slavery
summary: The National Convention abolished slavery in all French colonies and granted citizenship to formerly enslaved people.
reason: The slave revolt in Saint-Domingue and the arrival of its deputies in Paris pushed the Convention to act.
significance: It was the first general abolition of colonial slavery by a European power, though Napoleon restored it in 1802.

title: Eli Whitney patents the cotton gin
summary: Eli Whitney received a US patent for a machine that quickly separated cotton fibres from their seeds.
reason: Short staple cotton could grow across the American South, but removing its seeds by hand was slow.
significance: It made cotton hugely profitable and greatly expanded slavery in the United States.

title: Robespierre falls on 9 Thermidor
summary: The National Convention turned on Maximilien Robespierre and his allies, who were arrested and guillotined the next day.
reason: Deputies feared they would be the next victims of the Terror.
significance: It ended the Reign of Terror.

title: France adopts the metric system
summary: A French law defined the metre, the gram and the litre as the new national units of measure, with decimal multiples.
reason: Revolutionaries wanted rational, universal units to replace hundreds of local measures.
significance: The metric system became the international standard.

title: Edward Jenner tests the first vaccine
summary: Edward Jenner inoculated eight year old James Phipps with material from a cowpox sore. The boy later proved immune to smallpox.
reason: Jenner had heard that milkmaids who caught cowpox did not get smallpox.
significance: It founded vaccination, which later eradicated smallpox.

title: Mungo Park reaches the Niger River
summary: Scottish explorer Mungo Park reached the Niger at Segou and saw that it flowed east.
reason: The African Association in London sent him to trace the course of the river.
significance: It answered a long standing geographic question and opened European exploration of West Africa.

title: Napoleon defeats the Mamluks at the Battle of the Pyramids
summary: Napoleon Bonaparte's army defeated the Mamluk cavalry of Murad Bey near Cairo.
reason: France invaded Egypt to threaten British routes to India and spread French influence.
significance: It gave France control of Egypt and began intense European engagement with the Middle East.

title: Nelson destroys the French fleet in the Battle of the Nile
summary: Horatio Nelson's fleet attacked the French fleet at anchor in Aboukir Bay and destroyed most of it.
reason: Britain had hunted the fleet that carried Napoleon's army to Egypt.
significance: It stranded Napoleon's army in Egypt and restored British naval supremacy in the Mediterranean.

title: Tipu Sultan dies as Seringapatam falls
summary: British and allied forces stormed Seringapatam, capital of Mysore. Tipu Sultan was killed defending it.
reason: The East India Company feared Tipu's alliance with revolutionary France.
significance: It removed the most dangerous opponent of British power in southern India.

title: Ranjit Singh captures Lahore
summary: The young Sikh chief Ranjit Singh took Lahore, which became the capital of his rising state.
reason: He was uniting the rival Sikh misls of the Punjab under his rule.
significance: It laid the foundation of the Sikh Empire.

title: French soldiers discover the Rosetta Stone
summary: Soldiers of the French expedition found a stone inscribed in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek scripts near the town of Rashid.
reason: They were rebuilding a fort during the French occupation of Egypt.
significance: It became the key to deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphs.

title: Napoleon seizes power in the coup of 18 Brumaire
summary: Napoleon Bonaparte and his allies overthrew the Directory and set up the Consulate, with Napoleon as First Consul.
reason: The Directory was unpopular, corrupt and unable to end war and instability.
significance: It ended the revolutionary decade and began Napoleon's rule.

title: Alessandro Volta announces the electric battery
summary: Alessandro Volta described his voltaic pile, a stack of metal discs and brine soaked cloth that produced a steady electric current, in a letter to the Royal Society.
reason: Volta set out to disprove Galvani's theory that electricity came from animal tissue.
significance: It gave science its first source of continuous current and opened electrochemistry.

title: Giuseppe Piazzi discovers Ceres
summary: At the Palermo observatory, Giuseppe Piazzi found a moving object between Mars and Jupiter, the first known asteroid.
reason: Astronomers were searching for a planet predicted to lie in the gap between Mars and Jupiter.
significance: It revealed the asteroid belt.

title: Napoleon and the Pope sign the Concordat of 1801
summary: France and Pope Pius VII agreed to restore the Catholic Church's legal position in France, with the state naming bishops.
reason: Napoleon wanted to end the religious conflict of the Revolution and win over Catholic France.
significance: It shaped church and state relations in France for a century.

title: The United States buys Louisiana from France
summary: American envoys in Paris signed a treaty to buy the vast Louisiana territory from France for about 15 million dollars.
reason: Napoleon needed money for war and had lost hope of a New World empire after the failure in Saint-Domingue.
significance: It roughly doubled the size of the United States.

title: Haitians defeat the French at the Battle of Vertieres
summary: Jean-Jacques Dessalines's army defeated the French at Vertieres near Cap-Francais, forcing the French to leave Saint-Domingue.
reason: Napoleon had sent an expedition to restore French control and slavery.
significance: It ended the war of independence and cleared the way for Haiti.

title: Haiti declares independence
summary: Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed the independence of Haiti at Gonaives.
reason: Former slaves had defeated the French army sent to restore slavery.
significance: Haiti became the first independent Black republic and the first nation to abolish slavery permanently.

title: First railway journey by a steam locomotive
summary: Richard Trevithick's steam locomotive hauled iron and passengers along the tramway of the Penydarren ironworks in Wales.
reason: Trevithick had developed high pressure steam engines and wanted to prove they could pull loads on rails.
significance: It was the first locomotive to haul a train on rails, the start of railways.

title: France enacts the Napoleonic Code
summary: The French Civil Code, drafted under Napoleon, came into force, setting uniform laws on property, contracts and the family.
reason: France had a patchwork of local customs and royal law that the Revolution wanted to replace.
significance: It became the model for civil law in much of the world.

title: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French
summary: In Notre-Dame de Paris, in the presence of Pope Pius VII, Napoleon placed the imperial crown on his own head.
reason: Napoleon wanted to make his rule hereditary and give it the prestige of monarchy.
significance: It ended the First Republic and created the First French Empire.

title: US Marines attack Derna in the First Barbary War
summary: A small force of US Marines and mercenaries led by William Eaton attacked and captured Derna in Tripolitania.
reason: The United States was at war with Tripoli over the tribute demanded from American ships.
significance: It was the first US land battle overseas and is remembered in the Marines' Hymn.

title: Nelson wins the Battle of Trafalgar
summary: A British fleet under Horatio Nelson defeated the combined French and Spanish fleet off Cape Trafalgar. Nelson was killed.
reason: Napoleon's fleet was trying to gain control of the seas for operations against Britain.
significance: It ensured British naval supremacy for a century and ended any threat of a French invasion of Britain.

title: Napoleon wins the Battle of Austerlitz
summary: Napoleon defeated the larger armies of Austria and Russia near Austerlitz in Moravia.
reason: The Third Coalition had formed against Napoleon's growing power in Europe.
significance: It destroyed the Third Coalition and made Napoleon master of central Europe.

title: British win the Battle of Blaauwberg at the Cape
summary: A British force defeated the Batavian garrison north of Cape Town, leading to the surrender of the Cape Colony.
reason: Britain wanted to secure the sea route to India from Napoleon's Dutch allies.
significance: It began British rule in South Africa.

title: Holy Roman Empire is dissolved
summary: Emperor Francis II abdicated the imperial title and released the states of the empire from their duties, ending the Holy Roman Empire.
reason: Napoleon's victories and the creation of the Confederation of the Rhine had made the empire powerless.
significance: It ended a political order that had lasted about a thousand years.
wikipedia: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire

title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
summary: The Slave Trade Act received royal assent, prohibiting the slave trade in the British Empire.
reason: Decades of campaigning by abolitionists such as William Wilberforce and Thomas Clarkson won over Parliament.
significance: Britain then used its navy to suppress the Atlantic slave trade.

title: Fulton's steamboat sails up the Hudson
summary: Robert Fulton's North River Steamboat left New York City for Albany, making the trip in about 32 hours.
reason: Fulton and Robert Livingston sought a monopoly on steam navigation on the Hudson.
significance: It began commercially successful steam navigation.

title: Rum Rebellion deposes Governor Bligh
summary: Officers of the New South Wales Corps arrested Governor William Bligh and took over the colony.
reason: Bligh had clashed with powerful officers and settlers over trade, land and rum.
significance: It is the only successful armed takeover of government in Australian history.

title: Portuguese royal court arrives in Rio de Janeiro
summary: Prince Regent John and the Portuguese court reached Rio de Janeiro, which became the capital of the Portuguese Empire.
reason: The royal family fled Lisbon to escape Napoleon's invasion of Portugal.
significance: It transformed Brazil and led directly to its independence.
wikipedia: Transfer of the Portuguese court to Brazil

title: May Revolution sets up a junta in Buenos Aires
summary: Residents of Buenos Aires removed the Spanish viceroy and installed the Primera Junta.
reason: Napoleon's capture of the Spanish king left the colonies questioning who held authority.
significance: It began the independence of Argentina.
place: Plaza de Mayo, Buenos Aires, Argentina

title: Bogota rises against Spanish rule
summary: A quarrel over a borrowed flower vase sparked a revolt in Santa Fe de Bogota, and creole leaders set up a junta.
reason: Creoles resented Spanish power and saw an opening in the crisis of the Spanish monarchy.
significance: It is celebrated as the start of Colombia's independence.

title: Miguel Hidalgo issues the Cry of Dolores
summary: Priest Miguel Hidalgo rang the church bell in Dolores and called on his parishioners to rise against Spanish rule.
reason: Discovery of an independence plot forced Hidalgo to act at once.
significance: It started the Mexican War of Independence.

title: Chile forms its first national government junta
summary: An open council in Santiago replaced the Spanish governor with a junta.
reason: With the Spanish king captive, Chilean creoles chose self government in his name.
significance: It began Chile's road to independence and is its national day.

title: Muhammad Ali massacres the Mamluks in Cairo
summary: Muhammad Ali, governor of Egypt, invited Mamluk leaders to the Cairo Citadel and had them killed.
reason: He wanted to eliminate the Mamluks as rivals to his power.
significance: It gave him unchallenged control of Egypt and opened his modernising reign.

title: Venezuela declares independence
summary: A congress in Caracas declared Venezuela independent of Spain.
reason: Revolutionaries such as Francisco de Miranda and Simon Bolivar pushed for a full break with Spain.
significance: It was the first independence declaration in Spanish America.

title: Earthquake destroys Caracas
summary: A strong earthquake struck Caracas and other Venezuelan towns on Holy Thursday, killing thousands.
reason: It was caused by movement along fault lines in northern Venezuela.
significance: Royalist clergy called it divine punishment, which helped bring down the First Republic of Venezuela.

title: Spanish Cortes proclaims the Constitution of 1812
summary: The Cortes of Cadiz, meeting in a city besieged by the French, proclaimed a liberal constitution for Spain and its empire.
reason: With the king held by Napoleon, Spanish patriots set out to rebuild the nation on new principles.
significance: It became a model for liberal constitutions in Europe and Latin America.

title: Napoleon crosses the Neman to invade Russia
summary: The Grande Armee, over 400,000 strong, began crossing the Neman River into the Russian Empire.
reason: Russia had abandoned Napoleon's Continental System against British trade.
significance: The invasion ended in disaster and broke Napoleon's power.

title: Battle of Borodino
summary: Napoleon's army fought Kutuzov's Russian army at Borodino west of Moscow in one of the bloodiest single days of battle in history.
reason: Kutuzov made a stand to defend Moscow against the invading French.
significance: Napoleon took Moscow but his army was too weakened to win the war.

title: Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice is published
summary: Thomas Egerton published Pride and Prejudice in London, without naming its author.
reason: Austen had revised an earlier draft after the success of Sense and Sensibility.
significance: It became one of the most loved novels in English.

title: Battle of the Nations begins at Leipzig
summary: The armies of Russia, Prussia, Austria and Sweden began a three day battle against Napoleon at Leipzig, the largest in Europe before the First World War.
reason: After the Russian disaster, the allies united to drive Napoleon out of Germany.
significance: Napoleon's defeat cost him Germany and led to his first abdication.

title: Congress of Chilpancingo declares Mexican independence
summary: The Congress of Anahuac, convened by Jose Maria Morelos, signed the first formal declaration of Mexico's independence from Spain.
reason: Morelos sought to give the insurgency a government and a political program.
significance: It was the first official declaration of Mexican independence.
wikipedia: Solemn Act of the Declaration of Independence of Northern America

title: Napoleon abdicates in the Treaty of Fontainebleau
summary: Napoleon agreed with the allies to give up the French throne in exchange for sovereignty over Elba.
reason: Allied armies had taken Paris and his marshals refused to fight on.
significance: It ended the First French Empire and restored the Bourbon monarchy.

title: Kandyan Convention ends the Kingdom of Kandy
summary: Kandyan chiefs and the British signed an agreement placing the Kandyan Kingdom under the British Crown.
reason: The chiefs had turned against their king, and the British had occupied Kandy.
significance: It brought all of Sri Lanka under British rule.

title: Mount Tambora erupts
summary: Mount Tambora on Sumbawa erupted with enormous force, the largest eruption in recorded history.
reason: Pressure built inside the volcano for years before the climactic explosion.
significance: Ash in the atmosphere caused the Year Without a Summer in 1816, with famine across the Northern Hemisphere.

title: Congress of Vienna signs its Final Act
summary: European powers signed the Final Act of the Congress of Vienna, redrawing the map of Europe after the Napoleonic Wars.
reason: The victors wanted a balance of power that would prevent another French domination.
significance: It shaped a European order that largely kept the peace among great powers for decades.

title: Napoleon is defeated at Waterloo
summary: The Duke of Wellington's allied army and Blucher's Prussians defeated Napoleon at Waterloo.
reason: Napoleon had returned from Elba and tried to strike before the allies could unite.
significance: It ended the Napoleonic era.

title: Brazil is raised to a kingdom equal to Portugal
summary: Prince Regent John created the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves, ending Brazil's colonial status.
reason: With the court in Rio, the crown wanted a dignified status for Brazil and a strong position at the Congress of Vienna.
significance: It was a key step toward Brazilian independence.
